For students planning to study in the UK, the confusing part is often not the English test itself. It is working out which universities accept it and whether the same rules apply to every course.

If you are looking for an OIETC accepted university in UK, you will find plenty of names online. Some are current. Some are not. University policies change, and the terminology has changed too.

This OIETC accepted university list in UK brings the important information together for students preparing for 2027 entry. You will find current university examples, OIETC terminology, accepted countries, score guidance, test fees and the checks worth making before you book anything.

What Does OIETC Mean?

OIETC commonly refers to Oxford International English Test Centre.

You may still see this name on UK university English-language requirement pages. For example, the University of Hertfordshire lists OIETC among its accepted English qualifications, while UCLan London describes it as the English Language Level Test delivered by Oxford International Digital Institute.

Today, the test is more commonly presented under the Oxford ELLT name.

So you may come across several terms:

  • OIETC
  • Oxford International ELLT
  • Oxford ELLT
  • English Language Level Test
  • ELLT

They can appear on different university websites depending on how that institution describes the qualification.

Do not dismiss a university page simply because it uses OIETC rather than Oxford ELLT. Check the university's latest English-language requirements and make sure the qualification and score shown apply to your course.

If you are comparing several ways to prove your English ability, it may help to understand the English-language requirements commonly used by UK universities.

According to the official Oxford ELLT university partner directory, more than 100 UK universities and higher education institutions currently recognise the test. The worldwide partner network includes more than 300 institutions.

The full UK list is longer than this. But a name in a directory should be the beginning of your check, not the end of it.

Imagine that you want to apply to two universities. Both appear to accept the test. One may accept the online version, while the other may expect a test-centre version. Your required score may also change from one course to another.

That is why it is worth checking the course before paying for the test.

If you need detailed university-specific ELLT scores and Digital or Global requirements, see our guide to UK universities that accept Oxford ELLT.

UK Universities That Still Use the OIETC Name

Although Oxford ELLT is now the more familiar branding, some universities still use OIETC in their admissions information.

University of Hertfordshire

The University of Hertfordshire's current English-language requirements list Oxford International English Test Centre (OIETC) among its accepted qualifications.

For an IELTS 6.0 equivalent profile, Hertfordshire lists:

  • overall grade B2+
  • B2 in each skill

For an IELTS 6.5 equivalent profile, it lists:

  • overall grade C1
  • B2 in each skill

This is a useful example because it shows why old articles quoting scores such as 70, 80 or 100 can cause confusion. Always use the score format shown by the university you are applying to.

UCLan London

The English-language requirements at UCLan London currently refer to Oxford International English Test Centre, OIETC, delivered by Oxford International Digital Institute.

For its standard undergraduate English profile, UCLan London currently asks for Grade 6 overall with no component below Grade 5.

That is much more useful than relying on a generic minimum score copied from an older university list.

University of Greenwich

The University of Greenwich publishes Oxford International ELLT requirements alongside an OIETC equivalency table.

For an IELTS 6.0 profile with 5.5 in each skill, Greenwich currently lists OIETC 6 overall with a minimum 5 in each skill. For an IELTS 6.5 profile with 5.5 in each skill, it lists OIETC 7 overall with a minimum 5 in each skill.

There is an important exception for Bangladeshi students.

Greenwich currently states that this Oxford International English Language Level Test is not available to Bangladesh, and Bangladeshi nationals cannot use it as an IELTS waiver.

So even when a university accepts the test, the same option may not be available to every applicant.

University of Westminster

The University of Westminster's English-language requirements use the Oxford ELLT name.

It currently accepts both ELLT Digital and ELLT Global, but applicants from Bangladesh, India and Pakistan are strongly recommended to take ELLT Global at an approved test centre.

For Bachelor's courses requiring IELTS 6.0 overall, Westminster currently uses ELLT Grade 6 overall with Grade 5 in each skill.

Many Master's courses requiring IELTS 6.5 use ELLT Grade 7, although component requirements can vary.

For a student applying from Bangladesh, this is exactly the kind of detail worth checking before booking.

OIETC Accepted Country List

OIETC is recognised by institutions in several countries, but universities decide whether they accept the test. There is no blanket rule saying that every university in an accepted country must recognise it.

So, which countries accept OIETC?

Students currently have options in:

  • the United Kingdom
  • Canada
  • the United States
  • several European countries
  • other destinations within the wider partner network

But an OIETC accepted country does not mean every university in that country accepts it.

For example, knowing that more than 70 Canadian institutions recognise the test tells you that Canada may be worth considering. You would still need to check the individual college or university before applying.

OIETC Scores and the Current ELLT Scale

One of the biggest problems with older OIETC information is the scoring.

You may still find articles suggesting that undergraduate students need an OIETC score of 70 to 80 or that postgraduate applicants need 80 to 100.

That is not the current Oxford ELLT scoring system.

Oxford ELLT now assesses candidates on a 13-level OIDI scale from 0 to 12 for reading, listening, writing and speaking, as well as the overall result. The scores can be mapped against IELTS and CEFR levels.

A useful part of the current comparison looks like this:

So, if your university asks for an English level equivalent to IELTS 6.0, ELLT Level 6 is a common reference point.

There is a catch.

The overall score may not be enough.

A university can ask for Level 6 overall and still require a minimum score in every individual skill. UCLan London, for instance, currently requires Grade 6 overall with no component below Grade 5 for its standard undergraduate profile.

Always check both.

Is OIETC Accepted for 2027 Entry?

Yes, students planning 2027 entry can already find many UK institutions that recognise the test.

The safer approach, though, is to treat current requirements as your planning information rather than assuming that every policy will remain unchanged until your course starts.

University English requirements can change. Course-specific requirements can change too.

A sensible process is:

  1. Shortlist the universities you want.
  2. Check their current English requirements.
  3. Confirm the requirement for your exact course.
  4. Check again before booking the test.
  5. Recheck the condition when you receive your offer.

Students aiming for an early start may also want to compare UK universities with January entry.

If you are planning for the main autumn cycle, see how September entry works at UK universities.

How Much Does OIETC Cost?

Students looking for the OIETC test will now usually book it under the Oxford ELLT name.

The current standard prices are:

Test

Current Price

Oxford ELLT Digital

£120

Oxford ELLT Global

£120

Oxford ELLT Digital can be taken online from home, while ELLT Global is taken at an authorised test centre. Standard results are normally available within 48 hours.

For eligible candidates, Oxford ELLT also offers Skill Retake.

Skill Retake

Current Fee

Reading

£50

Listening

£50

Writing and Speaking

The official Skill Retake guidance says eligible candidates have 10 days after receiving their results to book a retake. The new score replaces the original score for that skill, even if the new result is lower.

That final detail is easy to miss. A retake does not let you keep whichever result is higher.

How Long Is an OIETC Result Valid?

Oxford ELLT currently states that the test result is valid for 18 months from the date it is issued.

This is another area where older information can be misleading.

Some old OIETC guides say results remain valid for two or three years. Do not rely on that figure for the current test.

A university may also have its own rule about how recent your English-language evidence must be. Check both the test validity and the university's admission requirement.

Why You Should Check Old OIETC Lists Carefully

University policies do not stay the same forever.

The previous version of this article listed more than 50 institutions, including Kingston University.

It also told students that undergraduate programmes might require scores of 70 to 80 and postgraduate programmes 80 to 100.

The FAQ said ELLT scores were typically valid for two to three years.

Those are exactly the kinds of details worth rechecking rather than carrying forward year after year.

A university may stop accepting a test. Another may add it. Digital and test-centre rules can change. Country restrictions can change too.

So when you find an old university list online, use it to start your research, not to make your final decision.

How to Check Whether a University Accepts OIETC

You do not need a complicated process.

Start with the university's English-language requirements page.

Confirm the qualification and then check your course.

Look for:

  • the required overall score
  • minimum scores in individual skills
  • whether Digital or Global is accepted
  • country-specific restrictions
  • how recent the result must be
  • any separate requirements for a pre-sessional course

For example, a Bangladeshi student looking at Westminster should notice the university's recommendation to take ELLT Global. A Bangladeshi student looking at Greenwich has a different issue because Greenwich currently says the test is not available to Bangladesh.

Those details can save you from paying for the wrong test.

If you are still comparing several routes, you may also want to look at UK study options without relying only on IELTS.

OIETC Is Not the Oxford Test of English

The word Oxford can cause confusion here.

OIETC and Oxford ELLT relate to Oxford International Digital Institute.

The Oxford Test of English is a different English-language qualification.

Do not assume that a university accepting one automatically accepts the other.

If you see an admissions page mentioning an Oxford test, read the full test name before using it as evidence for your application.

It sounds obvious, but it is an easy mistake to make when several similarly named tests appear in the same search results.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the OIETC full form?

OIETC commonly refers to Oxford International English Test Centre. Some UK universities still use this name in their English-language requirements, while the test is now more commonly presented under the Oxford ELLT branding.

Which university accepts OIETC in UK?

Current examples include the University of Hertfordshire, University of Greenwich, University of Leeds, University of Plymouth, University of Reading, University of Westminster, University of Surrey and University of York. Always check the requirement for your individual course.

How many universities are on the OIETC accepted university list in UK?

Oxford ELLT currently says more than 100 UK universities and higher education institutions recognise the test.

Is there an OIETC accepted university in UK for 2027 entry?

Yes. Students planning 2027 entry currently have many UK institutions to consider. Check the university's latest course requirements again before applying or booking the test.

Which countries accept OIETC?

Institutions in the UK, Canada, the United States and several European countries currently recognise Oxford ELLT. Oxford ELLT reports more than 300 partner institutions worldwide.

What is the OIETC accepted country list?

Current Oxford ELLT figures show more than 100 recognised UK institutions, more than 70 in Canada, more than 90 in the United States and more than 20 in non-UK Europe.

What OIETC score is equivalent to IELTS 6.0?

Under the current Oxford ELLT scoring scale, ELLT Level 6 corresponds to IELTS 6.0. Your university may also require minimum component scores.

How much does OIETC cost?

Oxford ELLT Digital and Oxford ELLT Global currently cost £120 each.

How long is an OIETC result valid?

Oxford ELLT currently states that its result is valid for 18 months from the date of issue.

Can I retake one ELLT skill?

Eligible candidates can retake Reading, Listening, or Writing and Speaking together. Current prices are £50 for Reading, £50 for Listening and £70 for Writing and Speaking.

Before You Book the Test

An OIETC accepted university list can help you narrow down your options, but the final decision should always come from the university's current requirements.

Check the university. Then check your course.

If you are still deciding where to study, you can also explore UK study options for international students while building your shortlist. Your supplied static-page list confirms this is one of your existing relevant pages.
